item.title: The First Sci-Fi Book Haul of the Second Half of This Year Has Arrived
item.author: Author
item.description: The batch is Mission of Gravity, The Martian Chronicles and True Names. Mission of Gravity uses that cover — and wow, that illustration is from some old issue of Science Fiction World. Even back then I was wondering how a plane like that flies. No engine — is it a glider? No idea whether it has anything to do with the novel. Word is this book is hard core. So I bought it.

item.title: Book Review: Marooned in Realtime
item.author: Author
item.description:
http://book.douban.com/review/3801851/

“Marooned in Realtime” is obviously the sequel to “The Peace War”. The style is different — Realtime reads a lot like a detective novel — but I don’t think the way it’s told is all that different. Vinge’s novels always spend a huge amount of the early going laying out the setting, the characters, the clues and so on, so with a Vinge novel you have to get at least halfway through before it becomes impossible to put down. “Realtime” and “The Peace War” are both like that, and so was “A Fire Upon the Deep”, which I read before: the beginning was so dull, I spent days on the first half, reading a bit and stopping, and then I finished the second half in one sitting. The real climax is at the back. It makes you not want to put it down.

item.title: Starting the Hyperion Sequel, Endymion
item.author: Author
item.description:
The full set of original editions arrived right after New Year, and I never got a chance to read them. I’d meant to start from the first book, but I found the plot had lost its freshness, and reading it in English made it hard to keep going, so I decided to start straight from the sequel.

Two days in, I’ve read two pages and run into a pile of unfamiliar words. Still, it’s not too bad — without a dictionary I can more or less guess the plot, and with a dictionary I get it properly. But if you asked me to translate the whole thing into Chinese, I don’t think I’m up to it. Right now I’m stuck at the beginner stage of “getting the gist”.
